Zhabokrych Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Zhabokrych's Jewish community began with just 6 families recorded in 1765, later growing to over 1,300 by 1897, about a fifth of the town's population. Under Romanian occupation, murders took place at three separate sites within the town over July 27–29, 1941; some who were wounded managed to escape. That winter, 245 Jewish deportees from northern Bukovina and Bessarabia were resettled into the empty houses of the local Jews murdered that July, joining roughly 200 survivors of the massacre in a newly established ghetto marked by appalling, disease-ridden conditions.
